title: Japanese Language — N4 to N3 Conversation and Natural Speech
description: Closes the gap between reading N3 Japanese and speaking and hearing it naturally. Students master the casual speech layer (contractions, sentence-final particles, discourse markers), build a working command of the three-tier keigo system, train listening comprehension at natural conversational speed through shadowing, and learn to express uncertainty, nuance, and emotion with the evidential vocabulary that makes Japanese sound like a native rather than a textbook.
learning_outcomes: Recognize and produce the core casual speech contractions (てる, とく, ちゃう, んだ, じゃない, なきゃ) in appropriate contexts
Use sentence-final particles (ね, よ, よね, な, かな, ぞ, ぜ, わ, さ, し, もん) with correct register and gender awareness
Deploy discourse markers and filler words (えーと, あの, まあ, なんか) and aizuchi naturally in conversation
Navigate the three-tier keigo system — teineigo, sonkeigo, kenjōgo — and produce the 15 core irregular keigo verb pairs correctly
Hear and parse natural Japanese speech at 5-7 mora/second using shadowing and intensive listening techniques
Recognize connected speech phenomena (vowel devoicing, mora compression, sentence-final truncation) so familiar words are not lost at natural speed
Choose the correct evidential/uncertainty expression from the certainty spectrum: かもしれない, らしい, ようだ, みたいだ, そうだ (appearance vs. hearsay), はずだ, に違いない
Use softeners (ちょっと, なんか, まあ), discovery expressions (なるほど, へえ), and indirect refusal strategies as fluent conversation management
research_notes: Tier 1 source available for keigo only (Agency for Cultural Affairs). Tier 2 academic sourcing for sentence-final particles (Saigo 2011) and shadowing effectiveness (Hamada 2016). Casual contractions and discourse markers rely on Tier 5 practitioner sources that are mutually corroborating. Pitch accent phonology and connected speech are established descriptive phonology but not available from web-fetchable Tier 1-2 sources.
